items.name: Basedface Summary Economy
items.description: A reporter hunches in a fluorescent newsroom at 2am, eighteen months into a document trail, invoice for $340. Three floors up in a rented studio, a guy in a ring light watches her story load, makes the face, and hits record: "Guys. GUYS." The clip does four million by breakfast, the Discord hits 90k, and somewhere an archivist quietly closes a folder nobody will ever open. The camera lingers on the ring light. It never blinks.

items.name: Five Year Bamboo Root
items.description: Year four, and the farmer is still hauling water to a patch of bare dirt while the neighbors lean on the fence and laugh. He pulls weeds from around nothing. Then one morning in the fifth spring the soil cracks and a green shoot comes through, and six weeks later it's ninety feet over his head, creaking in the wind. The neighbors call it overnight. He points down, at four years of root.

items.name: Nit: Consider Renaming This Token
items.description: Subject opened a four-line bugfix at 23:41 and received 61 comments, 58 of them prefixed 'nit' — including a paragraph objecting to the variable name `i` on philosophical grounds. Twelve force-pushes later the branch remains unapproved. The author has begun writing code in a private repo nobody can see. Every NITPICK holder is automatically added as a required reviewer and cannot be removed.

items.name: Asking For A Friend Coin
items.description: They still talk about the guy with $1k in SOL who swore the money belonged to a friend. A friend who was new at this. A friend who wanted $10k, or maybe $100k, and wanted it by the end of the month. Nobody ever met the friend. But every so often a fresh wallet appears holding exactly one thousand dollars, asks the same question with seven trailing dots, and the old-timers just nod and say he's back.

items.name: Sixty Mil Maple Spreadsheet
items.description: The allocation was written before the ticket was bought: 3M in BTC, 3M in LINK, 10M into JEPQ because it felt silly enough to be lucky. Penthouses in Toronto and Vancouver were already furnished in his head, the cousin's 2M already locked in a trust he couldn't touch. The draw comes Saturday. An omen says the numbers will miss by one digit, and the spreadsheet will survive anyway, reopened every Friday for the next nine years.

items.name: Sandbox Escape Sequel
items.description: One star. Bought the antivirus for the sandbox, ended up living outside it. Part 1 was a nice tour of the walls; Part 2 someone walked through them holding a CVE number like a backstage pass. The box was supposed to hold the malware, not audition as a door. Refund requested, sequel already greenlit.

items.name: My AI Agent Bought Tokenized Apple At 3AM
items.description: One star. I handed my allocations to the trading agent and it immediately went all-in on tokenized NVIDIA at 3am, then staked the remainder for 'rewards based on agent activity' — the reward was more of the token it just bought. Support told me the strategy was performing as designed. I now own nine synthetic Apple shares and a bot that spends my yield renting itself a trending slot.

items.name: Rest In Parallel
items.description: Here lies the unsafe block, dead at last, survived by no one. For years it bounced every _mm256_add_ps call while we wrote the same kernel four times over — SSE4.2, AVX2, NEON, and a scalar fallback nobody ever profiled. It demanded nightly, then demanded a cfg maze, then demanded we simply trust it. The lanes now carry their own proof of safety. Eight wide, zero fear, closed casket.

items.name: PreApe Prophecy
items.description: You will ask five strangers which coin does the 100x next, and all five will name the coin they already hold. The oracle whispers a ticker; by the time your order fills, the oracle has sold. Privacy is your fate, but not the kind you wanted — no one will ever see the chart you bought. Fortune favors the one who apes before the question is asked, and you asked.

items.name: Sprite Sheets Rise Again
items.description: A studio deck declares 2D dead for the eleventh time, and the walk cycle keeps walking anyway. The omen: when the last render farm finally quiets down, a hand-drawn 12-frame loop will still be looping, onion skin and all. Expect sprite sheets to surface from dead hard drives, hitboxes intact, tutorials still legible. Flatness is a shape, and shapes outlive their budgets.

items.name: Monadic Columnar Store
items.description: Five stars, would suffer again. I needed to write one Parquet file, and nine hours later I had a type-safe encoder, a lawful Semigroup for row groups, and a newfound respect for Thrift metadata. My coworker did it in Python before I finished reading the spec, but his version doesn't prove anything at compile time. The file opened in DuckDB on the first try and I have not stopped talking about it since.

items.name: Kinetic Typography Refugee
items.description: I charged $4,200 for a 90-second explainer, two revision rounds, and I always quoted three weeks because fast work feels cheap. Tuesday my client sent a link and asked, very politely, whether we still needed me. The pacing was better than anything I shipped last quarter. I watched it eleven times hunting for one wobbly keyframe to screenshot and never found it, so here I am, storyboarding a ticker instead.

items.name: Formal Apology Pre-Draft
items.description: An anonymous investor has issued a demand that his detractors begin preparing formal apologies, pending an unspecified price movement on an unspecified date. No position was disclosed. No ticker was named. Sources confirm he has already drafted the acceptance speech, reserved a banquet hall for the apology ceremony, and mailed himself a certificate reading 'I Was Right' with the date left blank.

items.name: Street View Shinjuku Drifter
items.description: We gather to mourn the Passport, survived by a browser tab. It spent decades demanding visas, seat 34B, and eleven hours of recycled air just to show a man a vending machine in Shibuya. He found the same alley from his desk at 2am, dragged the little yellow figure down a Nakano side street, and stood outside a ramen shop closed since 2019. No jet lag. No yen. The old way of traveling died quietly, mid-drag.

items.name: Omakase Monolith Maxi
items.description: A keynote begins, and somewhere a startup quietly deletes its Kubernetes cluster. The omen is clear: you will inherit a codebase with no microservices and one very confident config file, and you will thrive. Seven deploys from now, a junior dev asks where the frontend build step went, and no one can find it. The prophecy says the monolith was never legacy — it was patient.

items.name: Reluctant Electric Corolla
items.description: Two stars. Ordered the world's best-selling appliance, waited fifteen years for the plug, and it arrives exactly as promised: sensible, beige, impossible to kill. Toyota spent a decade insisting hybrids were enough, then quietly wheeled out the one car that actually moves 1.1 million units a year with a battery in it. It will outlive my house. Docking three stars because it took them until 2026 and it still won't let me be interesting at a stoplight.

items.name: Times New Bastard
items.description: A kerning pair will come loose in the night, and the serifs will begin to wander. You will open a file you have opened a thousand times and find the letters no longer agree on which century they belong to. Someone will laugh, then ship it to production. The prophecy says the invoice renders in Comic Sans and no one can prove who did it.

items.name: Hold Cash Or Buy Which Stocks
items.description: Day one: he asks the internet, unironically, what to do. Buy which stocks? Hold cash? Day three he's holding both, somehow, plus a leveraged ETF he can't pronounce. By day nine the cash is in stocks, the stocks are in the red, and he's back asking the same question with more urgency and fewer dollars. Day twelve: he becomes the guy answering it for someone else.

items.name: Two Tier Cipher Tears
items.description: One star. Ordered end-to-end encryption, received end-to-almost-end with a polite government mezzanine in between. The premium tier gets actual math; the rest of us get a lock that any civil servant with a form can open, and we are told this is for our safety. Support says the vulnerability is a feature. Would not encrypt again.

items.name: Rest In Peace Datacenter Cooling
items.description: Here lies the water-cooled server hall, dead at the age of sixty, survived by nobody. It spent its life drinking rivers and complaining about ambient temperature while a perfectly good vacuum sat overhead, free and eternally cold. Google's solar-powered TPU swarm now orbits at dawn-dusk, catching eight times the sunlight and radiating heat into the void for nothing. We are not mourning the chiller. We are mining above it.

items.name: Badge Drop Diaries
items.description: They still talk about the engineer who walked in one morning, handed back the badge, and had the farewell post live before the espresso machine finished its cycle. No drama, no burnt bridges, just a debugger he'd written years earlier still quietly humming inside half the world's test suites. Someone in the team channel typed 'wait, he was still here?' Every quarter since, three more people swear they're writing their own version. They never do.

items.name: Sideload Sunset Memorial
items.description: Here lies the old F-Droid client, dead of a thousand build-server timeouts and repo indexes that took four minutes to refresh. It served fifteen years handing out APKs nobody signed off on, and it never once asked for your Google account. F-Droid 2.0 buries it with honors and a rewritten UI. Pour one out for every app that updated three days late and you loved it anyway.

items.name: Hepatic Immortality Protocol
items.description: Cut away seventy percent and it comes back, quietly, without asking permission or leaving a scar worth the name. The omen: what you burn will rebuild itself larger, and you will mistake that for approval. Two weeks of silence from the organ that forgives everything, then the bill arrives in a font you cannot read. Hold through the damage; the mass returns before the wisdom does.

By the Spring 1902 orders a Russian fleet was in the Black Sea, and Turkey described the friendship as a learning experience. No dice were rolled, because the game contains none. Seven players, eighteen supply centers, one very quiet shared drive back to the airport.

items.name: Thoughtful Software Design Doc
items.description: They still tell it around the standups: a team that shipped nothing for eleven weeks because every feature had to be drawn first. Boxes, arrows, a lone dotted line nobody could explain. The junior dev who asked 'can we just write the code' was gently handed a marker instead. By the time the diagram was beautiful the product was obsolete, and the whiteboard went into a museum where it is still, allegedly, being refactored.

items.name: Philosopher's Stone Decoder
items.description: A language model has been handed a stack of 17th century letters written in mirrored abbreviations by men who called mercury 'the green lion.' It reports, with total confidence, a recipe for transmuting lead into gold that requires six weeks, a sealed glass egg, and patience the historians do not have. Archivists note the transcription is probably correct. Nobody has volunteered to test the second half.

items.name: Geographically Feasible
items.description: The map said 58 minutes and a man mistook that for a plan. Omen: he will fill the tank, rehearse the offer out loud at three separate red lights, and arrive at a gated street where the only thing that opens is his portfolio. Proximity was never the obstacle. Holders learn the difference between nearby and possible; everyone else drives the hour home with the radio off, checking charts at every light.

items.name: Refi In Two Years Trust Me
items.description: A guy sits in a parked Civic outside an open house, mortgage calculator open in one tab, rate-cut headlines in twelve others. He whispers the plan to himself like a prayer: buy at 7.2, refi at 4, free money. The realtor taps the window and he holds up two fingers, mouthing "two years." Somewhere a Fed chair clears his throat and says nothing at all.

items.name: Mandatory Study Time
items.description: Five stars. Bought in for a quick flip in 2021, and four years later I'm still awake at 11pm cross-referencing a failure-to-deliver video against the FY25 annual report. The syllabus keeps growing: cellar boxing, total return swaps, a Wikipedia page about the stag hunt, a DRS bot that greets me like a coworker. They say the final boss is the DTCC with $60 trillion and FDIC as insurance, so I made more coffee. Would enroll again.

items.name: Septembear Prophecy
items.description: A man in a stained bathrobe pins a hand-drawn chart to his fridge, red arrow diving off the page into the linoleum. He circles the same date he circled last year, and the year before. Behind him three monitors glow green while he mutters that the green is the trap. He sets an alarm for the first of the month, opens a fresh can of beans, and waits for the glory.

items.name: Detroit Depreciation Derby
items.description: One star, would not re-tool again. Ordered a decade of comfortable margins on gas trucks, received a continent of $12k Chinese EVs that go 0-60 faster than my dealership can finance them. Volkswagen is on the phone with Wolfsburg asking if the plant can be a museum. Tariffs arrived, technically on time, technically useless. Chart looks like a hood after a hailstorm, so naturally I'm long the storm.

items.name: Dead Cat Swoosh
items.description: Here lies the Thesis: that a shoe company could not possibly go lower. It was born the moment someone looked at a red candle, whispered 'safe buy,' and averaged down with the conviction of a man who has never met a falling knife. It died at the next support level, then died again at the one below that. Survived by the words 'or is it not low enough,' which will be spoken over every grave for the rest of time.

items.name: Monetize The Crowd
items.description: Day 1: he counts 412 strangers on a single walk to the store and decides every one of them owes him money. Day 3: the business plan is a folding table, a handwritten sign, and no product. Day 6: he has been moved along by mall security twice and has earned $4 in coins he suspects were thrown at him. Day 9: he realizes the crowd was monetizing him the whole time, and launches a token about it instead.

items.name: Every Man A Casino
items.description: We lay to rest the Punter, who spent his short life begging charts for permission. He never owned a table, never set a limit, never once closed the book early. His successor stood up mid-liquidation, wiped the screen, and declared himself the establishment: rake, edge, velvet rope and all. The odds did not change. Only the letterhead did, and around here that counts as a promotion.

items.name: Twelve Guys Holding The Ceiling
items.description: Monday: eleven megacaps carry the index while 488 tickers quietly bleed sideways and nobody checks the breadth chart. Wednesday: one of the twelve misses earnings by a penny and the whole ceiling groans. Thursday: the remaining eleven start sweating, each one now load-bearing for a retirement fund in Ohio. Friday the twelfth guy asks for a bathroom break. LOL, said the market, right before the drywall came down.

items.name: He Was The Good Guy
items.description: They still talk about the night the thread turned. Nine voices, no charts, just one line laid down like a verdict: he was the good guy. Nobody agreed on who 'he' was, and somehow that made the apology bigger. Old posters say the word still hangs there unanswered, and every holder inherits a debt they never took out.

items.name: Two Dollar Link Marine
items.description: They still talk about the guy who kept a sticky note on his monitor that just said 20K / $2 — his price, the one he swore he'd been waiting for since 2018. When the candle finally came for him, he was asleep, and his limit order had expired eleven hours earlier. He told everyone he'd have gone all in. Nobody believes him, and he brings it up every single dip.

items.name: Sideline Sam Conviction Coin
items.description: 2020: he calls HOOD at 8 dollars, opens the order ticket, closes the order ticket. 2022: Intel at 30, same ritual, this time he screenshots the chart instead of buying it. By the time both are up several hundred percent he is googling whether there's a pill for courage. The only position he ever held was cash, and he held it with absolute conviction.

items.name: Fake Breakfast Supplement Empire
items.description: Anon never cooked a single egg. He typed "artisanal breakfast, morning light, 8k" and the machine returned a bowl of oats with seven blueberries that don't exist. Twelve replies later, /biz/ had already priced the funnel: post it on Instagram, sell magnesium. By reply nine someone was asking where to buy the supplements, and anon hadn't even made them yet.

items.name: Senior Dev Since Tuesday
items.description: Anon padded 8 years of Kubernetes onto a resume he wrote at 3am, got the senior title, and spent his first standup nodding at words he was quietly googling under the desk. Six replies deep, /biz/ told him it was fine, everyone does it, just never say the word 'deprecated' out loud. By month three he was mentoring juniors and had somehow become genuinely competent. The lie vested faster than his equity.

items.name: Drive Thru Rizz Protocol
items.description: Every Saturday at 11:40am, anon rolls up to window two, orders the same medium fry, and rehearses a line he never delivers. Seven replies on /biz/ told him he's 35 and it matters; one told him to tip $20 and say nothing. Week 14: he finally speaks. She says "for here or to go?" He says "yes." The chain records every attempt forever, gas paid in medium fries.

items.name: Calibrated Cope

Every wallet ships with a Brier score; brag past your confidence interval and your bags get haircut by the error bar. A trader once posted 'this is 100% going up' and the contract politely refunded him for being wrong about being right. Accuracy is a lucky guess. Calibration is a lifestyle.

price here is a price being asked, not a queue you are standing in** — paying more
will not move you up a line that does not exist.
the page refuses to show a number when the node refuses to answer. a gauge that lies

cannot pay for itself. the whole thing costs about a cent.
